**1. Introduction and Scope**

1.1 This manual establishes the eligibility criteria and procedures for certification under the Legal Aid Coordination Program. It applies to all applications received on or after January 15, 2024, and to all pending applications for which a determination has not yet been issued.

1.2 The Certification Review Board issues this manual pursuant to its authority under the program charter. The Board may issue supplementary guidance, interpretive memoranda, and procedural bulletins. In the event of a conflict between this manual and a supplementary document, the manual controls unless the supplementary document expressly states that it amends the manual.

1.3 Nothing in this manual creates an entitlement to certification. Certification is a determination of eligibility for program services and is subject to available funding and program capacity.

1.4 All staff involved in intake, eligibility determination, or review shall be familiar with this manual and shall apply its provisions uniformly. Questions regarding interpretation shall be directed to the Board through the designated program coordinator.

1.5 The Board may grant exceptions not otherwise provided for in this manual only through the formal waiver process described in Section 6. No staff member may waive a requirement informally.

Section 4: Asset Limits and Household Composition

4.1 General Asset Limit

The applicant's household must not hold countable assets exceeding the asset limit specified in this section. The asset limit is a single, uniform ceiling applied to the combined countable assets of all household members. Eligibility Policy Manual v4.2 asset_limit_household 5000 USD. Record status: current. This limit is effective as of the date of this manual revision and applies to all applications filed on or after the effective date.

The asset limit is applied as of the date the application is received. If the applicant's household exceeds the limit on that date, the application shall be denied unless an exclusion or exception under Section 4.4 or Section 4.5 applies. Eligibility specialists shall not consider assets acquired after the application date for purposes of the initial determination, except as provided in Section 4.6 regarding post-application changes.

4.2 Definition of Household

For purposes of this section, "household" means the applicant plus all persons who reside in the same dwelling unit and share income or expenses with the applicant. A person who resides in the same dwelling unit but maintains completely separate finances and does not share income or expenses shall not be counted as a household member, provided the applicant documents the separation.

4.2.1 Persons Always Counted. The following persons are always counted as household members, regardless of financial independence:

- The applicant's spouse, if the spouse resides in the same dwelling unit;
- Any minor child of the applicant who resides in the same dwelling unit, unless the child is in the legal custody of another person or agency;
- Any adult for whom the applicant or the applicant's spouse is the legal guardian or conservator.

4.2.2 Persons Presumed Counted. The following persons are presumed to be household members unless the applicant provides clear and convincing evidence that the person maintains separate finances:

- Parents or adult children of the applicant who reside in the same dwelling unit;
- Siblings of the applicant who reside in the same dwelling unit;
- Any other adult who resides in the same dwelling unit for more than six consecutive months.

The presumption in this subsection may be rebutted by documentation showing that the person does not share income or expenses with the applicant, such as a written rental agreement, separate bank statements, or separate utility accounts. The eligibility specialist shall weigh the totality of the evidence and shall document the basis for the determination.

4.2.3 Persons Not Counted. The following persons are not counted as household members:

- A tenant who pays fair market rent under a written lease;
- A boarder who pays for meals and lodging under a written agreement;
- A person who resides in the dwelling unit solely for caregiving purposes and does not share income or expenses;
- A person who is absent from the dwelling unit for more than 30 consecutive days, unless the absence is due to hospitalization, incarceration, or military service.

4.3 Countable Assets

Countable assets include all real and personal property owned by the household, except as excluded under Section 4.4. The value of an asset is its current fair market value minus any bona fide debts or encumbrances secured by the asset. For assets that are jointly owned with a person who is not a household member, only the household's proportional share of the net value shall be counted.

4.4 Exceptions and Special Circumstances

The Certification Review Board recognizes that strict application of the income and asset limits set forth in Sections 4.1 through 4.3 may, in certain circumstances, produce a result that is contrary to the purposes of the program. This Section describes the limited exceptions that may be granted and the documentation required to support each exception. Except as otherwise provided, all exceptions are discretionary. The eligibility specialist may grant an exception only when the applicant has submitted the documentation described below and the specialist has determined, in writing, that the exception is necessary and appropriate.

4.4.1 Victims of Domestic Violence

An applicant who is a victim of domestic violence may request an exception to the household composition rules in Section 4.2, the income counting rules in Section 4.1, or the asset limits in Section 4.3, where the application of those rules would require the applicant to count the income or assets of the abuser or would otherwise penalize the applicant for leaving the abusive household.

Eligibility. To qualify for this exception, the applicant must demonstrate that:

- The applicant is a victim of domestic violence, as defined in Section 2.1 of this Manual, and the abuse occurred within the 12 months preceding the application date, or the applicant is currently residing in a shelter or transitional housing program for victims of domestic violence; and
- The income or assets of the abuser would be counted as household income or assets under Sections 4.1 through 4.3; and
- Counting the abuser's income or assets would cause the household to exceed the applicable income or asset limit.

Documentation. The applicant shall provide at least one of the following:

- A sworn affidavit from the applicant describing the abuse, including the date(s) of the abuse and the identity of the abuser, signed under penalty of perjury;
- A police report, court order, or protective order related to the abuse;
- A letter from a domestic violence service provider, shelter, or transitional housing program confirming that the applicant received services related to the abuse; or
- A medical or mental health record documenting injuries or treatment related to the abuse.

The eligibility specialist may not require the applicant to obtain a police report or protective order as a condition of granting this exception. If the applicant cannot provide any of the documents listed above, the specialist shall accept a second affidavit from a person who has knowledge of the circumstances, such as a caseworker, clergy member, or treating professional.

Effect of Exception. When this exception is granted, the abuser's income and assets shall be excluded from the household's countable income and assets for the certification period. The applicant shall be treated as a household of one for purposes of determining the applicable income and asset limits, unless other persons are counted as household members under Section 4.2. The exception shall remain in effect for the duration of the certification period, unless the applicant voluntarily includes the abuser's income or assets in a subsequent application.

Example. An applicant resides with her abuser and their two children. The abuser earns $4,200 per month. The applicant has no income. Under the household composition rules, the abuser would be counted as a household member, and the household's income would exceed the limit for a household of four. The applicant submits a police report and a letter from a domestic violence shelter. The eligibility specialist grants the exception. The abuser's income is excluded, and the household is treated as a household of three (the applicant and two children). The household's countable income is $0, and the application is approved.
**Section 7. Documentation Requirements and Verification Procedures**

**7.1 General Requirements**

All applicants shall provide documentation sufficient to verify the information reported on the application form. Documentation must be legible, complete, and current as of the date of submission. The eligibility specialist shall review each document for authenticity and consistency with the application. Where a document is illegible, incomplete, or appears to have been altered, the specialist shall request a replacement or clarification before making a determination.

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, the applicant shall submit the documents listed in Section 7.2 within fifteen (15) calendar days of the date the application is filed. The specialist may grant one extension of up to fifteen (15) additional calendar days upon a finding of good cause. Good cause includes, but is not limited to, hospitalization, incarceration, a documented natural disaster affecting the applicant's area of residence, or the unavailability of a third-party record holder despite the applicant's diligent efforts to obtain the record. A request for extension shall be made in writing or orally during an interview and shall be documented in the case file.

The applicant bears the burden of providing all required documentation. The program shall not pay any fee charged by a third party for the production of a required document, except as provided in Section 7.5.

**7.2 Required Documents by Category**

The following documents shall be required, subject to the alternative and exception provisions of Sections 7.3 through 7.6.

*(a) Identity and Residency*

1. For each household member age eighteen (18) or older, one of the following:
   - A current, valid state-issued driver's license or identification card;
   - A current, valid U.S. passport or passport card;
   - A U.S. military identification card;
   - A permanent resident card (Form I-551); or
   - An employment authorization document (Form I-766) issued by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

2. For each household member under age eighteen (18), one of the following:
   - A birth certificate;
   - A U.S. passport or passport card;
   - A school record showing the child's name and date of birth; or
   - A medical record showing the child's name and date of birth.

3. Proof of current residency within the service area, which may include:
   - A current lease or rental agreement in the name of the applicant or another household member;
   - A current utility bill (electric, gas, water, or landline telephone) addressed to the applicant or another household member at the residence;
   - A current bank statement addressed to the applicant or another household member at the residence;
   - A current voter registration card; or
   - A letter from a homeless shelter or transitional housing program confirming the applicant's residence at the shelter, or a statement from the applicant describing the location where they are staying, if the applicant is experiencing homelessness.

*(b) Income*

1. For each household member age eighteen (18) or older with earned income, the following, covering the most recent four (4) consecutive weeks prior to the date of application:
   - Pay stubs or earnings statements from each employer; or
   - If pay stubs are not available, a letter from the employer on company letterhead stating the employee's rate of pay and hours worked for the relevant period, or a written statement from the applicant explaining the absence of pay stubs, together with any other available evidence of earnings, such as bank deposit records.

2. For each household member with self-employment income:
   - The most recent federal income tax return, or, if not yet filed, a signed statement of anticipated income for the current year, together with profit-and-loss records, receipts, or other business records for the most recent three (3) months.
**Section 7: Application Processing and Decision Timelines**

**7.1 General Processing Standards**

The Certification Review Board (CRB) shall process every complete application in accordance with the timeframes set forth in this Section. These timeframes are measured in business days, which are defined as Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays and any additional closure days announced by the CRB. All timeframes begin on the date the application is deemed complete, as described in Section 7.3 below.

The CRB recognizes that timely decisions are essential to the effective delivery of legal aid services. Accordingly, the CRB shall allocate sufficient staff to meet the processing standards in this Section, and the Executive Director may temporarily reassign eligibility specialists to the intake team during periods of high application volume.

**7.2 Intake Steps**

Upon receipt of an application, intake staff shall perform the following steps in the order listed:

1.  **Date-Stamp and Log.** Immediately upon receipt, whether by mail, fax, in-person drop-off, or electronic submission, the application shall be date-stamped and entered into the case management system. The system shall assign a unique application number, which shall be used for all subsequent correspondence and records.

2.  **Initial Completeness Review.** Within two (2) business days of receipt, an intake coordinator shall review the application to determine whether all required fields on the application form have been completed and whether all documents listed in Section 6 (Documentation Requirements) have been submitted. If the application is incomplete, the intake coordinator shall send a written notice to the applicant listing the missing items. The applicant shall have fifteen (15) business days from the date of the notice to submit the missing items. If the applicant fails to do so, the application shall be administratively closed, and the applicant shall be so notified in writing.

3.  **Assignment to Eligibility Specialist.** Once an application is deemed complete, it shall be assigned to an eligibility specialist within one (1) business day. Assignments shall be made on a rotating basis, except that applications involving allegations of domestic violence or other emergency circumstances, as identified by the intake coordinator, shall be assigned to the next available specialist immediately.

4.  **Conflict of Interest Check.** Prior to beginning the substantive review, the assigned eligibility specialist shall review the application to determine whether any conflict of interest exists, including any personal or financial relationship between the specialist and the applicant or any household member. If a conflict is identified, the specialist shall promptly return the application to the intake coordinator for reassignment to another specialist.

**7.3 Determination of Application Completeness**

An application is deemed complete when all of the following conditions are met:

- The application form is fully completed and signed by the applicant or the applicant's authorized representative;
- All documentation required under Section 6 has been submitted;
- The applicant has provided a current mailing address and, if available, a telephone number and email address; and
- The applicant has not been determined ineligible for a period that has not yet expired, as set forth in Section 9 (Reapplication and Ineligibility Periods).

**Appendix B: Glossary of Terms**

For purposes of this Manual, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms not defined in this Glossary shall have their ordinary meaning, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.

**Adjusted Gross Income (AGI)** – The applicant’s gross income minus allowable deductions, as reported on the most recent federal income tax return, or as calculated using the Income and Expense Declaration (Form EL-102) if no tax return was filed.

**Applicant** – The individual who submits an application for legal aid services on their own behalf or on behalf of a household member.

**Asset** – Any real or personal property owned by the applicant or any household member, including but not limited to cash, bank accounts, stocks, bonds, retirement accounts, real estate, vehicles, and other items of value. See Section 4 for exclusions.

**Authorized Representative** – An individual who has been designated in writing by the applicant to act on the applicant’s behalf in connection with an application for legal aid. The designation must be made on Form EL-100 or by separate written authorization.

**Business Day** – Any day on which the Eligibility Program office is open for business, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays observed by the office.

**Certification Review Board** – The body responsible for adopting and revising this Manual and for reviewing eligibility determinations upon appeal.

**Conflict of Interest** – A situation in which an eligibility specialist, or a member of the specialist’s immediate family, has a personal or financial relationship with the applicant or any household member that could reasonably be perceived as affecting the specialist’s impartiality.

Section 4: Asset Limits and Household Composition

4.1 General Asset Limit

The applicant's household must not hold countable assets exceeding the asset limit specified in this section. The asset limit is a single, uniform ceiling applied to the combined countable assets of all household members. Eligibility Policy Manual v4.2 asset_limit_household 5000 USD. Record status: current. This limit is effective as of the date of this manual revision and applies to all applications filed on or after the effective date.

The asset limit is applied as of the date the application is received. If the applicant's household exceeds the limit on that date, the application shall be denied unless an exclusion or exception under Section 4.4 or Section 4.5 applies. Eligibility specialists shall not consider assets acquired after the application date for purposes of the initial determination, except as provided in Section 4.6 regarding post-application changes.

4.2 Definition of Household

For purposes of this section, "household" means the applicant plus all persons who reside in the same dwelling unit and share income or expenses with the applicant. A person who resides in the same dwelling unit but maintains completely separate finances and does not share income or expenses shall not be counted as a household member, provided the applicant documents the separation.

4.2.1 Persons Always Counted. The following persons are always counted as household members, regardless of financial independence:

- The applicant's spouse, if the spouse resides in the same dwelling unit;
- Any minor child of the applicant who resides in the same dwelling unit, unless the child is in the legal custody of another person or agency;
- Any adult for whom the applicant or the applicant's spouse is the legal guardian or conservator.

4.2.2 Persons Presumed Counted. The following persons are presumed to be household members unless the applicant provides clear and convincing evidence that the person maintains separate finances:

- Parents or adult children of the applicant who reside in the same dwelling unit;
- Siblings of the applicant who reside in the same dwelling unit;
- Any other adult who resides in the same dwelling unit for more than six consecutive months.

The presumption in this subsection may be rebutted by documentation showing that the person does not share income or expenses with the applicant, such as a written rental agreement, separate bank statements, or separate utility accounts. The eligibility specialist shall weigh the totality of the evidence and shall document the basis for the determination.

4.2.3 Persons Not Counted. The following persons are not counted as household members:

- A tenant who pays fair market rent under a written lease;
- A boarder who pays for meals and lodging under a written agreement;
- A person who resides in the dwelling unit solely for caregiving purposes and does not share income or expenses;
- A person who is absent from the dwelling unit for more than 30 consecutive days, unless the absence is due to hospitalization, incarceration, or military service.

4.3 Countable Assets

Countable assets include all real and personal property owned by the household, except as excluded under Section 4.4. The value of an asset is its current fair market value minus any bona fide debts or encumbrances secured by the asset. For assets that are jointly owned with a person who is not a household member, only the household's proportional share of the net value shall be counted.

4.4 Exceptions and Special Circumstances

The Certification Review Board recognizes that strict application of the income and asset limits set forth in Sections 4.1 through 4.3 may, in certain circumstances, produce a result that is contrary to the purposes of the program. This Section describes the limited exceptions that may be granted and the documentation required to support each exception. Except as otherwise provided, all exceptions are discretionary. The eligibility specialist may grant an exception only when the applicant has submitted the documentation described below and the specialist has determined, in writing, that the exception is necessary and appropriate.

4.4.1 Victims of Domestic Violence

An applicant who is a victim of domestic violence may request an exception to the household composition rules in Section 4.2, the income counting rules in Section 4.1, or the asset limits in Section 4.3, where the application of those rules would require the applicant to count the income or assets of the abuser or would otherwise penalize the applicant for leaving the abusive household.

Eligibility. To qualify for this exception, the applicant must demonstrate that:

- The applicant is a victim of domestic violence, as defined in Section 2.1 of this Manual, and the abuse occurred within the 12 months preceding the application date, or the applicant is currently residing in a shelter or transitional housing program for victims of domestic violence; and
- The income or assets of the abuser would be counted as household income or assets under Sections 4.1 through 4.3; and
- Counting the abuser's income or assets would cause the household to exceed the applicable income or asset limit.

Documentation. The applicant shall provide at least one of the following:

- A sworn affidavit from the applicant describing the abuse, including the date(s) of the abuse and the identity of the abuser, signed under penalty of perjury;
- A police report, court order, or protective order related to the abuse;
- A letter from a domestic violence service provider, shelter, or transitional housing program confirming that the applicant received services related to the abuse; or
- A medical or mental health record documenting injuries or treatment related to the abuse.

The eligibility specialist may not require the applicant to obtain a police report or protective order as a condition of granting this exception. If the applicant cannot provide any of the documents listed above, the specialist shall accept a second affidavit from a person who has knowledge of the circumstances, such as a caseworker, clergy member, or treating professional.

Effect of Exception. When this exception is granted, the abuser's income and assets shall be excluded from the household's countable income and assets for the certification period. The applicant shall be treated as a household of one for purposes of determining the applicable income and asset limits, unless other persons are counted as household members under Section 4.2. The exception shall remain in effect for the duration of the certification period, unless the applicant voluntarily includes the abuser's income or assets in a subsequent application.

Example. An applicant resides with her abuser and their two children. The abuser earns $4,200 per month. The applicant has no income. Under the household composition rules, the abuser would be counted as a household member, and the household's income would exceed the limit for a household of four. The applicant submits a police report and a letter from a domestic violence shelter. The eligibility specialist grants the exception. The abuser's income is excluded, and the household is treated as a household of three (the applicant and two children). The household's countable income is $0, and the application is approved.

**7.1 General Requirements**

All applicants shall provide documentation sufficient to verify the information reported on the application form. Documentation must be legible, complete, and current as of the date of submission. The eligibility specialist shall review each document for authenticity and consistency with the application. Where a document is illegible, incomplete, or appears to have been altered, the specialist shall request a replacement or clarification before making a determination.

Except as otherwise provided in this Section, the applicant shall submit the documents listed in Section 7.2 within fifteen (15) calendar days of the date the application is filed. The specialist may grant one extension of up to fifteen (15) additional calendar days upon a finding of good cause. Good cause includes, but is not limited to, hospitalization, incarceration, a documented natural disaster affecting the applicant's area of residence, or the unavailability of a third-party record holder despite the applicant's diligent efforts to obtain the record. A request for extension shall be made in writing or orally during an interview and shall be documented in the case file.

The applicant bears the burden of providing all required documentation. The program shall not pay any fee charged by a third party for the production of a required document, except as provided in Section 7.5.

**7.2 Required Documents by Category**

The following documents shall be required, subject to the alternative and exception provisions of Sections 7.3 through 7.6.

*(a) Identity and Residency*

1. For each household member age eighteen (18) or older, one of the following:
   - A current, valid state-issued driver's license or identification card;
   - A current, valid U.S. passport or passport card;
   - A U.S. military identification card;
   - A permanent resident card (Form I-551); or
   - An employment authorization document (Form I-766) issued by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

2. For each household member under age eighteen (18), one of the following:
   - A birth certificate;
   - A U.S. passport or passport card;
   - A school record showing the child's name and date of birth; or
   - A medical record showing the child's name and date of birth.

3. Proof of current residency within the service area, which may include:
   - A current lease or rental agreement in the name of the applicant or another household member;
   - A current utility bill (electric, gas, water, or landline telephone) addressed to the applicant or another household member at the residence;
   - A current bank statement addressed to the applicant or another household member at the residence;
   - A current voter registration card; or
   - A letter from a homeless shelter or transitional housing program confirming the applicant's residence at the shelter, or a statement from the applicant describing the location where they are staying, if the applicant is experiencing homelessness.

*(b) Income*

1. For each household member age eighteen (18) or older with earned income, the following, covering the most recent four (4) consecutive weeks prior to the date of application:
   - Pay stubs or earnings statements from each employer; or
   - If pay stubs are not available, a letter from the employer on company letterhead stating the employee's rate of pay and hours worked for the relevant period, or a written statement from the applicant explaining the absence of pay stubs, together with any other available evidence of earnings, such as bank deposit records.

2. For each household member with self-employment income:
   - The most recent federal income tax return, or, if not yet filed, a signed statement of anticipated income for the current year, together with profit-and-loss records, receipts, or other business records for the most recent three (3) months.

**Section 7: Application Processing and Decision Timelines**

**7.1 General Processing Standards**

The Certification Review Board (CRB) shall process every complete application in accordance with the timeframes set forth in this Section. These timeframes are measured in business days, which are defined as Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays and any additional closure days announced by the CRB. All timeframes begin on the date the application is deemed complete, as described in Section 7.3 below.

The CRB recognizes that timely decisions are essential to the effective delivery of legal aid services. Accordingly, the CRB shall allocate sufficient staff to meet the processing standards in this Section, and the Executive Director may temporarily reassign eligibility specialists to the intake team during periods of high application volume.

**7.2 Intake Steps**

Upon receipt of an application, intake staff shall perform the following steps in the order listed:

1.  **Date-Stamp and Log.** Immediately upon receipt, whether by mail, fax, in-person drop-off, or electronic submission, the application shall be date-stamped and entered into the case management system. The system shall assign a unique application number, which shall be used for all subsequent correspondence and records.

2.  **Initial Completeness Review.** Within two (2) business days of receipt, an intake coordinator shall review the application to determine whether all required fields on the application form have been completed and whether all documents listed in Section 6 (Documentation Requirements) have been submitted. If the application is incomplete, the intake coordinator shall send a written notice to the applicant listing the missing items. The applicant shall have fifteen (15) business days from the date of the notice to submit the missing items. If the applicant fails to do so, the application shall be administratively closed, and the applicant shall be so notified in writing.

3.  **Assignment to Eligibility Specialist.** Once an application is deemed complete, it shall be assigned to an eligibility specialist within one (1) business day. Assignments shall be made on a rotating basis, except that applications involving allegations of domestic violence or other emergency circumstances, as identified by the intake coordinator, shall be assigned to the next available specialist immediately.

4.  **Conflict of Interest Check.** Prior to beginning the substantive review, the assigned eligibility specialist shall review the application to determine whether any conflict of interest exists, including any personal or financial relationship between the specialist and the applicant or any household member. If a conflict is identified, the specialist shall promptly return the application to the intake coordinator for reassignment to another specialist.

**7.3 Determination of Application Completeness**

An application is deemed complete when all of the following conditions are met:

For purposes of this Manual, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms not defined in this Glossary shall have their ordinary meaning, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.
